API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (th
e same server without `/api/v1`)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved
before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with

exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads resu
lts) decides its server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL
` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the tw
o variables naming different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not
a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command ex
its `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON re
port, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credential
s are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Usi
ng MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` red

acts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `

project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most r
ecently updated project you can see\n\nEmpty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** se

lect a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpj
am cloud link # writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: cred

ential, deployment, selector
mcpjam cloud eval list # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud
eval` run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `vid
eo`) follow the same rule — `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-proj

ect listing and cannot be combined with `--project`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means
\

n`--host` is not one flag. The meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `re
sources`, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, a
nd protocol version in `initialize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, t
ool visibility and model settings. Never the real client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default i
s all. |\n| `cloud eval --host`, `cloud goals`, `cloud studies` | A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-name>`), the client config an
eval or goal run is stamped with. |\n| `cloud environments --host-id` | The project Host id the environment runs as. Distinct from
eval's `--host`. |\n\n`--host` on a local command is mutually exclusive with `--client-capabilities`. A Cloud `--host` is mutuall

y exclusive with `--server` / `--environment` when those already supply a closed server set.

## Global flags

These flags app
ly to every command. Cloud credentials `--api-key` / `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not the program root.\n\n| Flag |

Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--timeout <ms>` | `30000` | Request timeout in milliseconds |
| `--rpc` | off | Inclu
de raw JSON-RPC request/response logs in JSON output under `_rpcLogs` |\n| `--quiet` | off | Suppress non-result progress output o
n stderr |\n| `--no-telemetry` | off | Disable anonymous telemetry for this invocation |\n| `--format <format>` | `human` on TTY,

`json` when piped | Raw output format (`json` or `human`) |
| `-v, --version` | | Print the CLI version |

## Output formats
\
nThe CLI auto-detects whether stdout is a terminal:\n\n* **Interactive terminal** — defaults to `--format human`. For most command
s this is pretty-printed JSON; `server doctor` and the OAuth conformance commands provide dedicated human-readable summaries.\n* *
*Piped or redirected** (CI, `| jq`, agent invocation) — defaults to `--format json`, the full structured result.\n* **Conformance
in CI** — `protocol conformance`, `protocol conformance-suite`, `oauth conformance`, `oauth conformance-suite`, `apps conformance`
, and `apps conformance-suite` support `--reporter junit-xml` and `--reporter json-summary`.\n* **Explicit `--format`** always win
s over the auto-detected default.\n\n**For agents**: raw JSON is the source of truth. Human format is a lossy presentation layer.
If you're parsing output programmatically, pass `--quiet --format json`.\n\nJSON-valued flags accept inline JSON, `@path`, or `-`
for stdin. `tools call` also accepts `--tool-args-stdin` as a shorthand for `--tool-args -`. Use files or stdin for large payloads

url $URL --access-token $TOKEN \
 --tool-name my_tool --tool-args - --quiet --format json
```

## Connecting to servers

T

he CLI supports two transport modes, selected by which flags you pass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP.
* `--command ...` selects s
tdio.\n* `--transport http|stdio` is optional and acts as an explicit override/validator when you want the CLI to reject mismatche

d flags early.

### HTTP (Streamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --url http

s://your-server.com/mcp
```

Add auth when needed:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# Static bearer token
mcpja

m server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a prior login
mcpjam server doctor

--url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server

.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

### Stdio (local subprocess)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam

server doctor --command node --args server.js --cwd /path/to/project -e API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

Stdio child processes inherit t
he parent shell environment by default. Use\n`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones for the spawned server.\nStructur
ed debug artifacts only record the explicit env keys you pass through\n`-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.\n

> [!NOTE]
>
> `oauth ...` and `protocol ...` are HTTP-only command groups. They do
> not accept stdio targets.

## Update n
otifications\n\nAfter a successful command, the CLI checks whether a newer version of `@mcpjam/cli` is available and prints a noti

ce to stderr when one is found:

```
Update available: @mcpjam/cli 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
Run npm install -g @mcpjam/cli to update
``
`\n\nThe check is non-blocking: version data is fetched in a detached background process and cached locally for 24 hours, so it ne
ver slows down your commands. The notice is written to stderr only and never touches stdout or JSON output, so it is safe for both
interactive terminals and AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that capture stderr. It is suppressed automatically in CI.\n\nTo
